description.narrative:
Programme Focus:
Impact area 1: Women lead, participate in and benefit equally from governance systems • 1.1: Women engage in political institutions and processes. • 1.2: National and Local Plans and budgets are gender responsive • 1.3: Policy and Financial Environment to track GEWE • 1.4: Gender statistics to monitor policies and reporting commitments under SDGs • 1.5: Gender statistics used by different players to inform advocacy, policies and programmes
Impact area 2: Women have income security, decent work and economic autonomy • 2.1: Public and private procurement is gender responsive, • 2.2: Climate smart agricultural policies are gender responsive and womens land tenure security is increased.
Impact area 3: All women and girls live a life free from all forms of violence • 3.1: An enabling legislative and policy environment in line with international standards on EVAWG, Womens Access to Justice, and other forms of discrimination is in place and translated into action, • 3.2: Favorable social norms, attitudes and behaviors are promoted at community and individual levels to prevent VAWG and end child marriage, • 3.3: Increased use of available accessible and quality essential services by women and girls who experience violence.
Impact area 4: Women and girls contribute and have a greater influence in building sustainable peace and resilience, and benefit equally from the prevention of natural disasters and conflicts and from humanitarian action • 4.1: More commitments on women, peace and security are implemented by GoU and the UN, and more gender equality advocates influence peace and security processes, • 4.2: Women benefit from Humanitarian action in the context of refugee response.
ORGANIZATIONAL DEVELOPMENTS • More effective and efficient UN system coordination and strategic partnerships on gender equality and women's empowerment, • Increased engagement of partners in support of UN Women's mandate, • High quality programmes through knowledge, innovation, results-based management and evaluation, • Enhanced organisational effectiveness, with a focus on robust capacity and efficiency at country and project level.

Sida ger stöd till UN Women i Uganda för att bidra till genomförandet av UNW:s landprogram ("UNW Uganda Country Office Strategic Plan and Programme 2019-2022"). Planen innefattar fyra tematiska områden och fyra interna organisationsutvecklingsområden:
1: Kvinnors möjlighet att leda, delta i och att dra likvärdig nytta av olika system för samhällsstyrning, 2: Kvinnors inkomstsäkerhet, rätt till anständigt arbete och ekonomisk självständighet, 3: Kvinnors och flickors rätt att leva ett liv fritt från alla former av våld, 4: Kvinnors och flickors möjligheter till inflytande för att bidra till hållbar fred och deras möjligheter att dra lika nytta av förebyggande arbete avseende naturkatastrofer och konflikter samt av humanitära insatser. • Mer effektiv samordning och fler strategiska partnerskap mellan FN-organisationer för att främja jämställdhet mellan kvinnor och män, • Ökat engagemang av partners för att stödja UNW:s mandat, • Program av hög kvalitet som bygger på kunskap, innovation, resultatbaserad ledning och utvärdering, • Förbättrad organisatorisk effektivitet med fokus på kapacitetsbyggande på land- och projektnivå.
Sida tillhandahåller icke-öronmärkt stöd till UNW för att genomföra landprogrammet i Uganda under perioden 2020-2023. Flera givare bidrar till UNW:s verksamhet i Uganda, främst genom projektstöd.

UNW has requested support for the implementation of the UN Women Country Office Strategic Plan and Programme 2019-2022 in Uganda. The country programme is aligned with the UNDAF/UNSDCF in Uganda and the national development plan, national legislation and policies for gender equality, and the global UN Women strategy. It focuses on four thematic areas and four areas of organisational effectiveness and efficiency; 1: Women lead, participate in and benefit equally from governance systems, 2: Women have income security, decent work and economic autonomy, 3: All women and girls live a life free from all forms of violence, 4: Women and girls contribute and have a greater influence in building sustainable peace and resilience, and benefit equally from the prevention of natural disasters and conflicts, and from humanitarian action. • more effective and efficient UN system coordination and strategic partnerships on gender equality and women's empowerment, • Increased engagement of partners in support of UN Women's mandate, • High quality programmes through knowledge, innovation, results-based management and evaluation, • Enhanced organisational effectiveness, with a focus on robust capacity and efficiency at country and project level.
Sida provides non-earmarked support to UNW for implementing the programme in Uganda during the period 2020-2023. Several donors are funding UNW's operations in Uganda, primarily with project support.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
UN Women holds a strategic position in bridging the government and its partners at various levels. This role was a key rationale for including UN Women as a partner in the Strategy Portfolio in 2020, with the aim of mainstreaming gender equality. Sida assesses that UN Women has demonstrated capacity in fulfilling this role, with results during the final year of the agreement period deemed satisfactory. Notable achievements include successful advocacy efforts, the development of significant policy documents, and progress in activity-based initiatives. This is all in line with the objectives of the intervention.
Examples of results per impact area:
Impact Area 1: Inclusive Governance and gender sensitive peace and security
With its role as a facilitator to the government, UN Women and its partners have focused on enhancing governance by supporting the development and reinforcement of key legal and policy frameworks under this impact area. For example, UN Women's support has led to the development of progressive policy guidelines and a costed strategy for effective Gender Based Violence (GBV) management.
Within the justice system, UN Women's support has contributed to the creation of a survivors guide for navigating the criminal justice process and the establishment of standard service delivery guidelines for justice actors both of which have advanced victim friendly support for GBV survivors.
In terms of national monitoring and accountability, UN Women's support to the SDG Secretariat has led to a significant increase in Uganda's gender specific SDG reporting. The number of gender related indicators reported grew from 11 out of 54 in 2018 to 32 out of 54 in 2023. Overall, Uganda now has data for 54 out of 201 SDG indicators applicable to the country.
Impact Area 2: Shared Prosperity in a Healthy Environment for all Women & Girls
In 2023, UN Women Uganda expanded its engagement with the private sector to enhance its impact on women's economic empowerment. Additionally, UN Women strengthened its policy and programme advocacy around disaster risk reduction, with a focus on increasing the capacity of vulnerable women to mitigate and adapt to climate change and disaster risks. A total of 6,859 women farmers across Kiryandongo, Nakivale, Nwoya, and Bugiri districts demonstrated improved skills in climate smart agriculture. In Nwoya district alone, 4,500 women cultivated climate resilient fruits, while in Bugiri, 1,400 women adopted climate resilient technologies in aquaculture through cage fish farming.
Impact Area 3: Human Well-Being and Resilience
Through capacity building and technical support, along with improvements in the quality and integrity of forensic evidence submitted by police officers, UN Women support has contributed to more trauma informed approaches within the justice system. This has resulted in an increased number of cases being sanctioned through prosecutor led investigations and higher conviction rates in SGBV special sessions from 80 percent in 2022 to 82 percent in 2023.
UN Women has also placed emphasis on the inclusion of persons with disabilities. In collaboration with its partners, UN Women provided technical assistance to the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (MGLSD) in developing a comprehensive guide to harmonize the implementation of disability related interventions within the context of social protection services. A National Plan of Action to operationalize the revised National Policy on Disability Inclusion was launched, disseminated, and rolled out in 30 districts.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
